title: Afternoon review: 'Place in a free block' menu opens BEHIND the review dialog, so it does nothing
detail: Daily Review > Afternoon > step 3 Time left. Pressing 'Place in a free block' sets aria-expanded=true and appends the menu panel to <body>, but the panel is z-index var(--z-menu)=110 while the review overlay is var(--z-modal)=120, so the menu is painted under the dialog's scrim and panel: nothing visible appears, and a tap where the item would be lands on the dialog (elementFromPoint at the first item's centre returns another row's 'Place in a free block' button). The item's onSelect itself works: invoking it programmatically creates the study block (15:30, 90 min, type study, assignmentId 1) with an Undo toast. Same root cause affects EVERY KOS.ui.menu used inside a KOS.ui.openDialog (the primitive never raises a menu above an open modal).
evidence: shots/productivity/dr-place-open-mac.png (menu open per aria-expanded, nothing shown); eval: panel z=110, overlay z=120, panel parent BODY, topEl at item centre = 'k-btn k-btn--sm ui.menu-button'; css/tokens.css:1031-1032 (--z-menu:110, --z-modal:120); css/components.css:334 (.k-menu-panel z-index var(--z-menu)); js/core/ui.js:813 (place() appends panel to document.body); js/modules/dayreview.js:609
fix: In KOS.ui.menu place(): when the button is inside an open dialog (btn.closest('[data-ui~="ui.dialog"], .k-dialog-overlay')), append the panel inside that overlay (or set a state the CSS maps to z-index above --z-modal, e.g. a --z-menu-modal token 130). Add a smoke test that opens a menu inside openDialog and checks elementFromPoint hits the item.
rootCause: Menu layer token (110) below the modal layer token (120); menus are portalled to body regardless of an open modal.

title: Afternoon review time strip: end label '22:00 夜' overprints the last hour tick; 30-minute block text wraps to two lines
detail: In the Time left strip the hour ticks are left-anchored at their position and run up to the last hour before the evening review, while the end label is pinned at inline-end. With from=04:46 and until=22:00 the 21:00 tick starts at ~94% of the width, exactly under '22:00 夜' (the screenshot shows '2̶2̶:̶0̶0̶' overprinted). Short free blocks (30 min = ~31px) wrap '30 min' onto two lines and overflow their outline. Same overlap happens at any width; worse on iPad portrait and phone where the strip is narrower.
evidence: shots/productivity/dr-afternoon-timeleft-mac.png (top-right of strip, and the 08:00 block); js/modules/dayreview.js:593-604 (tick loop t<to; tend appended unconditionally); css/views/routines.css:340-341
fix: Skip any tick whose position is within ~1 label width (e.g. >88%) of the end label, or render the end label as the final tick; thin ticks by available width (every 2h/3h below ~700px). For blocks narrower than the label, show the length only in the aria/tooltip or as a single-line '30m' with white-space:nowrap and no padding.
rootCause: No collision handling between left-anchored ticks and an inline-end end label; fixed hourly tick density regardless of width.

title: Every page header shows the PREVIOUS page's painted band after in-app navigation
detail: KOS.ui.pageHeader picks its art from KOS.store.state.ui.view, but KOS.show sets state.ui.view only AFTER the view function has rendered. So navigating Pacing -> Routines draws Pacing's band on Routines, Routines -> Focus draws Reminders' band (Routines maps to 'reminders') on the Focus Timer, Focus -> Reminders draws none (Focus has no PAGE_ART entry), etc. Only a reload (where ui.view was persisted) shows the right picture. Repro via eval navigating #/pacing,#/routines,#/focus,#/reminders,#/calendar,#/routines: header images were reminders, pacing, reminders, none, none, calendar respectively. Affects every page that uses pageHeader, not only Productivity; the art audit just released depends on it.
evidence: eval output: '#/pacing [app.hero.page.reminders.webp]', '#/routines [app.hero.page.pacing.webp]', '#/focus [app.hero.page.reminders.webp]', '#/routines [app.hero.page.calendar.webp]'; shots/productivity/focus-mac-seed.png and routines-mac-seed-2.png (sticky-note pinboard band on Focus/Routines); js/core/ui.js:589-592 (art = PAGE_ART[state.ui.view]); js/core/ui.js:1541-1543 (view rendered, then ui.view assigned)
fix: Set a module variable (e.g. KOS.ui.currentView = viewId) BEFORE calling KOS.views[viewId] and read that in pageHeader; or have each view pass opts.art explicitly. Add a smoke check: navigate A->B and assert B's band id.
rootCause: Ordering: state.ui.view is assigned after render in KOS.show (js/core/ui.js:1543), while pageHeader reads it during render.

title: Calendar has no Agenda (or Day) view on Mac or iPad; Agenda exists only under 700px
detail: At >700px the Calendar offers only Month and Week (js/modules/calendar.js:1545 mode is 'week'|'month'; buttons at 1589-1591). The Agenda list (renderPhone, the stored 'week' mode) is drawn only when matchMedia('(max-width:700px)') matches (calendar.js:1562-1563, 1613). So the user cannot get the agenda on the MacBook (1470) or iPad (820/1180). There is no Day view at any size. Also the same stored value calMode='week' means 'Week grid' on desktop and 'Agenda' on phone, so an iPad in Split View flipping across 700px silently changes view type.
evidence: shots/productivity/cal-week-mac.png, cal-week-ipad.png, cal-month-ipadl.png (segmented control: Month | Week only); shots/productivity/calendar-iphone-seed.png (Agenda | Month); js/modules/calendar.js:1545,1562-1563,1589-1591,1613-1620
fix: Make the mode a 3-value per-device setting {month, week, agenda} (+ optional day). Factor the phone agenda list (renderPhone's day lists + agendaRows) into a renderAgenda(board) usable at any width: on desktop/iPad draw it as the board beside the existing Today/Countdowns side column (a 2-week scrolling list grouped by day with time column, hue bar, derived chips). Keep phone default Agenda; migrate stored 'week' on phone to 'agenda'.
rootCause: Agenda was designed as the phone composition (frame 15g) and is hard-wired to the phone branch of render().

title: iPad portrait Calendar: '+ New event' wraps to its own row leaving a full-width empty band
detail: At 820px the header row (‹ title › Today Show Month|Week) fills the width and '+ New event' drops alone to a second line at the left, leaving ~600px empty beside it and pushing the grid down ~60px.
evidence: shots/productivity/cal-week-ipad.png (y≈235)
fix: Below 1080 put Today/Show on a second toolbar row with New event at its end, or collapse '+ New event' to the '+' icon button used on phone; or let the title shrink (clamp font-size) so the row fits.
rootCause: .k-cal-head is a wrapping flex row with no layout tier between desktop and phone.

title: Daily Review marks sit in the Week view's all-day row and their time is truncated away
detail: Review marks carry a time (Morning review · 07:00 etc.) but Week view lists them in the all-day row, where the 115px column truncates them to 'Morning revie…', so the time never shows; they also push every day's all-day row to 5-6 lines, shrinking the timed grid.
evidence: shots/productivity/cal-week-mac.png (all-day rows 5-6 chips tall); eval: 21 review chips at y 297-401; js/modules/calendar.js:600-606, 1799-1801
fix: Draw timed derived marks (reviews, routine windows) as thin dashed markers in the timed grid at their time, or as one compact '朝 昼 夜' glyph row per day with the times in the tooltip/aria.

title: Routine offer checkboxes render as 22x44 tall pills on touch devices
detail: In 'Start with these?' (Routines Today/Routines/Templates tabs) each pick box (.k-rt-check, routine.offer-pick) keeps its 22px width while the coarse-pointer rule raises its height to 44px, so on iPad and iPhone each checkbox is a white 22x44 capsule instead of a square. Invariant 69: a control raised for touch must raise its width too.
evidence: measure: 'SMALL button.k-rt-check[routine.offer-pick] 22x44' on ipad and iphone; shots/productivity/routines-iphone-seed.png (tall white capsules)
fix: Give .k-rt-check an explicit aspect-ratio:1 / inline-size equal to block-size under (pointer:coarse), or keep the visual 22px box and grow the hit area with the whole row as the label (the row is already a button-like card).
rootCause: Global coarse-pointer min-block-size for buttons without a matching min-inline-size on this control.

title: Routines 'Start with these?' card leaves ~400px dead on the right on Mac
detail: The offer card spans the full content width (1210px) but the illustration + a ~560px text/list column use only the left two thirds; the right ~400px is empty. Violates the no-dead-space rule.
evidence: shots/productivity/routines-mac-seed-2.png
fix: Either cap the card's width and place a second card beside it (e.g. Today's reviews), or lay the three template picks out as three columns across the width (they are short), or move the illustration to the right edge so the text sits between.

title: Routines: page-header 'Templates' button duplicates the Templates tab 60px below
detail: The page header's actions are 'Templates' and '+ New routine', and the tab strip right under it has a Templates tab going to the same place. Invariant 50b: never offer the same destination twice in-page.
evidence: shots/productivity/routines-mac-seed.png; js/modules/routines.js (routine.templates button)
fix: Drop the header 'Templates' button (keep + New routine), or drop the Templates tab and keep the button.

title: Daily habits card repeats the page sub-line, truncated, and has no add button when empty
detail: Routines Today: the Daily habits card heading's sub-line 'a habit is a routine with one …' is the page header's sub-line again and is ellipsised; empty it shows a paragraph and only a small 'Add habits ›' text link at top-right (on iPhone the link overlaps the truncated sub-line per measurement). Card height then leaves a dead lower half.
evidence: shots/productivity/routines-mac-seed-2.png (Daily habits card); measure iphone: 'OVERLAP span.k-rt-hd-m.k-ellipsis x button.k-link[routine.habits-edit]'; measure mac DEADH routine.habit-card used 95/244
fix: Remove the sub-line (or make it unique, e.g. 'tick-only, auto-tracked'), and in the empty state put a primary '+ Add a habit' button in the body.

title: Reminders: the right inspector column is a small hint card over a dead column
detail: With nothing selected, the 320px right column holds only 'Select a reminder to edit…' (120px tall) and is empty below for the whole list length.
evidence: shots/productivity/reminders-mac-seed.png, rem-today-mac.png
fix: When nothing is selected, collapse the inspector and let the list widen, or fill it with useful context (Today's count, upcoming this week, 'From your plan' summary, quick-add with date).

title: Reminders 'Today' leaves out overdue reminders
detail: Today shows 2 items while 8 reminders are overdue; they are only under Overdue/All. A user working from Today never sees what slipped. Most reminder apps (Apple Reminders) show overdue at the top of Today. Also 'From your plan' rows each carry a '↻ From your plan' chip under a 'FROM YOUR PLAN' heading (redundant), and the 'Open plan' links and priority chips sit on different right edges (≈1082 vs ≈1056).
evidence: shots/productivity/rem-today-mac.png; js/modules/reminders.js:334-349
fix: Include overdue items in Today under an 'Overdue' group (count it in the Today badge or show '2 + 8 overdue'); drop the per-row chip in the plan group; align the trailing column.

title: Focus: 'General study — no link' is overridden by About to Study, which silently links the session to the first assignment (even with 'Just start')
detail: On #/focus with subject 'General study — no link' and 'No assignment', pressing Start focus opens About to Study pre-filled with the overdue NEA assignment. Pressing 'Just start' (or Start Focus) starts a session with subject 'compsci' and assignmentId 1. The completed session then banks its minutes on that assignment (invariant 4a) and counts as CS study, i.e. time is misattributed. The only escape in the dialog, 'Change ▾', is a KOS.ui.menu that opens behind the dialog (same z-index bug), so there is no way to keep 'no link' short of turning off About to Study.
evidence: eval: Focus page left on General study/no assignment -> Start focus -> preflight.just-start -> session {subject:'compsci', assignmentId:1}; shots/productivity/focus-running-mac.png (About to Study shows NEA); js/modules/routineplayer.js:279-287 (taskOf falls back to taskChoices()[0] when ctx has no subject/assignment), 257 (go(skip) merges task even when skip); js/modules/focus.js:2253
fix: taskOf(ctx) must respect an explicit 'no link' from the Focus page: pass ctx.explicit = true from focus.js and return {title:'General study'} without falling back; offer the ladder's suggestion as a 'Use: <task>' choice instead of a default. 'Just start' should start exactly the Focus page's config (ctx without task). Fix the menu z-index too.
rootCause: taskOf() treats an empty subject as 'nothing chosen' and fills it from Today's three/assignments; go(true) still merges the filled task.

title: Running Focus: a long assignment title runs off the screen (left edge on Mac, right edge on iPhone)
detail: The objective/context column on the running Focus screen holds the assignment chip ('課 <title>') with no max width, wrapping or ellipsis. With the NEA assignment the k-fx-ctx box is 616px wide: on the Mac it starts at x=-131 (text cut at the window's left edge: 'tion: stakeholder interviews…'), on iPhone it ends at x=648 in a 402px viewport. The due date is printed raw ('due 2026-10-29'), as are the Focus page's assignment options ('· due 2026-10-29'). On iPhone the context card is also washed out over the bright window art (chips barely legible).
evidence: shots/productivity/focus-running-mac.png (left edge), shots/productivity/focus-running-iphone.png; eval: .k-fx-ctx rect x=-131..485 (mac), 32..648 (iphone, vw 402); js/modules/focus.js:879-883 (chip('課 '+asg.title), chip('due '+asg.due)), 1018, 2175; css/views/productivity.css:113-114
fix: Give .k-fx-ctx max-inline-size:100% (min-inline-size:0 on the column) and the chip a max-inline-size with text-overflow:ellipsis (title attr for the full name); format due with KOS.ui/hub dayLabel ('due Thu 29 Oct', 'overdue 4 d'). On phone put the context card on a stronger scrim (var(--s1) at ~80%).
rootCause: Chips are nowrap and the flex column is aligned to the end with no width cap, so long content overflows to the left (end-aligned) or right.

title: Focus page while a session is minimised is one banner over an empty page
detail: With a session running and minimised, #/focus shows only 'Session in progress — Computer Science' and 'Return to the stage →'; the rest of the 1210x500 content area is blank (Your record, The deal, today's sessions all disappear). Dead space and a lost chance to show live context (objective, cycle progress, notes, today's total).
evidence: shots/productivity/focus-page-minimised-mac.png
fix: Keep the idle page's right column (Your record with today's live total, The deal with the running session's live award preview from KOS.governor.focusAward) and in place of the setup card show a compact live card: clock, cycle bar, objective, Switch…, notes, End early/Return to the stage.

title: Session review repeats '36-day streak' four times and hides what the bonus gold was for
detail: Ending a Pomodoro paid +59 gold (5 for the session + 3+7+14+30 streak milestone bonuses that had not been recorded). The review and the toast print the note list '36-day streak · 36-day streak · 36-day streak · 36-day streak' and a single '+59 gold' while The deal had promised +5 gold, so the user cannot tell why. Each milestone pushes the CURRENT streak length as its note instead of the milestone it paid. The toast also sits over the review's 'Save review' button on Mac.
evidence: shots/productivity/focus-review-mac.png, focus-review-iphone.png; eval KOS.governor.lastAward() = {gold:59, notes:['36-day streak'×4]}; js/core/governor.js:330-338 (notes.push(stk + '-day streak'))
fix: Push one note per milestone: ms + '-day streak bonus +' + ms + ' gold' (or merge into one: 'Streak bonuses 3·7·14·30 days +54 gold'); show the session's own award and bonuses as separate lines in the review. Keep toasts above the dialog footer (offset by the footer height when a dialog is open).

title: Pacing week: lesson ticks (18x18) and lesson-day selects (62x24) are far below the 44px touch minimum on iPad/iPhone
detail: Every class lesson row's tick input (.k-pace-tick-in) measures 18x18 and its day <select> (pace.lesson-day) 62x24 at 820px and 402px with a coarse pointer; the week strip's scroller arrows are 32x32. On the iPad (the user's study device) these are the main controls of the page.
evidence: measure prod/m-ipad-__pacing.json, m-iphone-__pacing.json: 'SMALL input.k-pace-tick-in 18x18', 'SMALL select.k-pace-lesson-day 62x24', 'SMALL button.k-scroller-arrow 32x32'; shots/productivity/pace-week-iphone.png
fix: Make the whole lesson row a <label> for its tick (hit area = row height ≥44) and raise the day select to min-block-size 44px under (pointer:coarse) (or use the dense 24px-with-spacing exception explicitly, invariant 69).

title: Reminders: complete circles are 32x32 on touch
detail: The round complete button (rem.check) stays 32x32 with a coarse pointer on iPad and iPhone (invariant 69 asks 44 for coarse pointer, raising width with height for a circle). The sort/priority pill selects are 30px tall on iPad.
evidence: measure m-ipad-__reminders.json / m-iphone-__reminders.json: 'SMALL button.k-rem-check 32x32' (×28), 'SMALL select.k-pill-select 161x30'
fix: Under (pointer:coarse) give .k-rem-check a 44x44 hit box (visual circle can stay 22-24px via an inner span) and the pill selects min-block-size 44px.

title: Daily Review step tabs: the active tab's focus ring is clipped to two vertical crimson bars
detail: After a step tab is clicked, its focus outline renders only as two vertical crimson lines at its left and right (top and bottom are clipped by the step strip's overflow), which reads as a rendering glitch rather than a focus ring. Seen on Mac and iPad, in Afternoon and Evening reviews.
evidence: shots/productivity/dr-afternoon-timeleft-mac.png (around 'Time left'), dr-afternoon-ipad-empty.png, dr-evening1-mac.png (around 'Tomorrow')
fix: Use :focus-visible only (no ring after a pointer click) and an inset ring (outline-offset negative or box-shadow inset) so the scroller's overflow cannot clip it.

title: Evening review: 'Tomorrow's first task' says nothing is due while overdue plan rows exist; lesson rows show bare dashes
detail: In the evening review the first-task card reads 'Nothing is due soon, so tomorrow starts wherever you like.' although the afternoon review and Reminders list overdue carried-over plan rows; the candidates leave out Pacing rows. The card is then a tall empty box beside the timetable. Tomorrow's lessons with no class time print '–' in the time column.
evidence: shots/productivity/dr-evening1-mac.png; js/modules/dayreview.js:585 (empty-candidates text)
fix: Feed carried-over plan rows (KOS.pacing.dueThisWeek().carried) and the Focus ladder's next into the candidates; omit the time cell (or show 'lesson') when a lesson has no time.

title: Running Focus in a break: red 'End early' stays in the header beside 'End session'
detail: Once a Pomodoro cycle is banked, the stage shows '✓ End session' (pays +35 XP…) but the header still offers a red 'End early', so there are two end controls with conflicting wording and colour.
evidence: shots/productivity/focus-stage-break-mac.png
fix: Hide 'End early' (or relabel it 'End' in neutral style) when canComplete() is true.

title: Routines Today: three equal columns stretch the reviews and habits cards to the routine card's height
detail: With a routine due, Today's reviews (3 rows, ~200px of content) and Daily habits (one paragraph) are stretched to the Morning Routine card's ~460px, leaving large empty lower halves; the routine card's header is cramped ('Leave by 07:45 / 163 min from now' wraps to 4 lines while the side cards are empty).
evidence: shots/productivity/rt-today-mac.png
fix: Give the routine card 2 of 3 columns (or a full row) and stack reviews + habits in the third column; align-items:start for the side cards.

title: A routine whose steps are all optional can never be kept: ticking every step leaves it 'partial' for ever (no pay, no streak)
detail: verdict() counts only required steps and requires req.length > 0 for done, so a routine saved with every step marked Optional (the editor's per-step Optional switch allows it, and 'Ask the next morning' forces a step optional) is judged of=0: ticking both steps returns state 'partial', no award, and the day shows as partial in History and breaks the streak. The editor's save() only refuses zero steps.
evidence: eval prod2/rt1.js: R.add({steps:[{optional},{optional}]}) → tick both → {state:'partial', award:null}, verdict {done:false,n:0,of:0}; js/core/routines.js:316-323 (verdict: done = req.length > 0 && n === req.length); js/modules/routines.js:965-969 (Optional switch, checkMorning forces optional), 1039-1044 (save validates only step count)
fix: Either refuse to save (toast 'At least one step must be required') or judge an all-optional routine kept when every step (or any step) is ticked; the same rule in verdict() and the editor's total.
rootCause: verdict() has no rule for a routine with no required steps and the editor does not prevent one.

title: Ticking a routine's minimum step first pays the small minimum award and locks out the full award when you then finish every step
detail: pay() runs on the first tick that makes the day 'min' or 'done' and sets e.paid; routineAward gives a minimum day 5 XP/1 gold/2 HP. If the minimum step is ticked before the others (natural when it is the first or easiest step), the day is paid as a minimum; completing all three required steps afterwards turns the day 'done' but pays nothing more (award null), so the user receives less than if they had ticked the minimum last. The streak/verdict is right; the reward depends on tick order.
evidence: eval prod2/rt1.js: routine [full1, small(minimum), full2]: tick small → award {xp:5,gold:1,hp:2}, then tick full1 and full2 → state 'done', award null, sessions added still 1; js/core/routines.js:370-377 (pay when v.done||v.min and !e.paid), js/core/governor.js:124-131 (min → 5/1/2; 3 required → 11/1/3)
fix: Pay the difference when a 'min' day becomes 'done' (store e.paidAs = 'min' and top up once to the full award through one extra todo entry or by amending the award before the day closes), or pay a minimum only when the routine day ends without the full set.
rootCause: Pay-once is keyed to the first kept state rather than the best state reached that day.

title: '+ New routine' with a single step silently becomes a habit and disappears into Daily habits
detail: The routine editor's save() turns a NEW custom routine with one step into kind 'habit' (and normalise() names it after the step, ignoring nothing). After Save the app lands on the Routines tab, where the new routine is not listed: it is a row inside the Daily habits card on Today, with the routine's window/days applied as a habit. A user who started a one-step routine (e.g. 'Stretch, 5' with a 07:00–08:00 window) cannot find it where they made it, and its mark is dropped from view.
evidence: eval prod2/rtnew.js: #/routines {edit:'new'} → add step 'Stretch, 5' → Save → record {kind:'habit', name:'Stretch'}, location #/routines/routines and the tab text does not contain it; Today's habit card shows 'Daily habits 0 of 1 today … Stretch'; js/modules/routines.js:1045 (if steps.length === 1 && kind === 'custom' && isNew → kind 'habit'), 1047 (KOS.show('routines','routines') either way)
fix: Keep what the user made: save a one-step routine as a routine (kind custom) unless it was started from 'Add a habit'; if converting, say so in the toast ('Saved as a habit in Daily habits') and land on Today with the habit highlighted. The redundant ternary at 1047 shows the intended branch was never written.
rootCause: Implicit kind conversion on save with no feedback and a fixed landing tab.

title: Monthly reminders drift: due 31 Jan repeats 28 Feb, then 28 Mar (the day-of-month is lost after a short month)
detail: KOS.reminders.nextOccurrence advances from the PREVIOUS occurrence (clamped), so after one short month the repeat stays on the clamped day for ever: 31 Jan → 28 Feb → 28 Mar → 28 Apr. The Calendar's monthly recurrence anchors on the original day (occursOn: min(start day, last day)), so a reminder and a calendar event set up the same way disagree from March onwards. Yearly on 29 Feb has the same drift (to 28 Feb permanently).
evidence: eval prod2/rem.js: add({due:'2026-01-31',recur:'monthly'}) → nextOccurrence = '2026-02-28', next of that = '2026-03-28'; js/core/reminders.js:166-187 (addMonths clamps from `cur`), compare js/modules/calendar.js:422-428 (anchored to s.getDate())
fix: Store the anchor day (item.recurDay = original day of month, set when recur is chosen) and compute each next occurrence as min(anchor, last day of month), like the Calendar does.
rootCause: Recurrence is stepped from the last clamped date instead of the series' anchor.

title: Completing a repeating reminder cannot be undone and leaves no record: no Undo, un-tick does not restore the date, nothing in Completed
detail: Ticking a repeating reminder rolls its due date forward (skipping every missed occurrence) and clears done/completedAt. The row's tick has no Undo toast (unlike plan rows), the item never appears in Completed, and KOS.reminders.complete(id,false) only clears flags, so the old date is gone. The Daily Review's 'Done' for a repeating reminder shows an Undo that calls complete(id,false) and therefore does not undo anything. A mis-tap on 'Pay rent · monthly' silently moves it a month.
evidence: eval prod2/rem.js: weekly due 22 Oct → complete → due '2026-11-12', done false, completedAt null, not in query({section:'completed'}); complete(false) → due still '2026-11-12'; js/core/reminders.js:213-250 (roll forward, no history), js/modules/reminders.js:370-375 and 546/569 (tick → complete → draw, no toast/undo); js/core/dayreview.js:300 (undo = complete(id,false))
fix: Have complete() return the previous {due, alerted, subs} and offer an Undo toast that restores it; keep a small completion history on the item (completions: [ts…], last 20) so Completed and Reports can show 'done 3 times'.
rootCause: Recurrence mutates the record in place with no undo token or completion log.

title: Afternoon review 'Tomorrow' on a plan row says 'moved to tomorrow' when nothing moved
detail: In Time left, the place rows include up to two plan rows. Their 'Tomorrow' button calls triage(ref,'tomorrow'), which for a plan row writes nothing but returns {ok:true, note:'Plan rows stay in their week.'}; the button ignores the note and toasts '<title> · moved to tomorrow' with an Undo. The Evening review's triage step reads res.note (dayreview.js:532) but this button does not.
evidence: js/core/dayreview.js:314-319 (plan: no write, res.note), js/modules/dayreview.js:621 (toast 'moved to tomorrow' on r.ok, note ignored) vs 532 (note shown)
fix: Show r.note when present, or do not offer 'Tomorrow' for plan rows (offer 'Remind me tomorrow', which creates a reminder).
rootCause: Two callers of triage() handle its result differently.

title: Time-left strip's end label always reads the evening review time even when the strip runs past it (after ~21:00 two '22:00' labels, or the tick under the end label)
detail: timeStrip() ends the bar at max(evening time, start + 60 min) but always prints the evening time ('22:00 夜') at the right edge. After 21:00 the bar spans e.g. 21:20–22:20: an hour tick '22:00' is drawn at 67% AND '22:00 夜' at 100% (which is really 22:20); between ~21:00 and 21:10 the 22:00 tick lands under the end label (the overprint reported earlier). At 18:52 the strip is clean (ticks 19/20/21 at 248/588/927 px, end label 1210–1261 px).
evidence: eval prod2/place.js at 18:52: ticks [19:00 248-281, 20:00 588-621, 21:00 927-960], end 1210-1261; shots/productivity/inv/dr-time-mac.png; js/modules/dayreview.js:593-605 (to = Math.max(mins(until), from + 60); end label text = until)
fix: End the strip at the evening time (to = mins(until)) and when less than an hour is left draw it shorter, or label the end with the real end; skip an hour tick within ~40 px of the end label.
rootCause: The bar's span and its end label come from different values.

title: Review times can be set out of order and a later slot then folds a review that has not happened yet
detail: dayReview.normalise accepts any HH:MM per slot with no order check. With Morning at 19:00 and Afternoon at 16:30, due() at 17:00 offers the Afternoon review with folded:['morning'], i.e. a morning review two hours in the future is marked folded (and will not open at 19:00 either, since the afternoon iterates later).
evidence: eval: setConfig({slots:{morning:{weekday:'19:00'}}}) → due(17:00 Mon) = {slot:'afternoon', folded:['morning']}; js/core/dayreview.js:90-100 (no ordering), 166-176 (due iterates slots in fixed order)
fix: Clamp in the gate (morning < afternoon < evening, at least 30 min apart) and say so in Settings next to the time inputs; or have due() fold only slots whose time has passed.
rootCause: The settings gate validates each time alone.

title: Auto-tracked Focus habits count aborted sessions and split a late-night session at midnight instead of at the routine day start
detail: autoMeasure() sums every focus entry's stretches for the day, including incomplete sessions that pay nothing (a 9-minute early stop added 9 min: 19 → 28), so three aborted 9-minute starts tick a '25 min of Focus' habit. It also filters by the ledger's calendar day (e.date === day) while `day` is the ROUTINE day (04:00 start, invariant 148): a session from 23:30 to 00:30 is split between two calendar days, and between 00:00 and 04:00 the minutes count towards the next routine day, not the night they belong to.
evidence: eval prod2/auto.js: baseline focus/maths today 19 min → after pushing an incomplete 540 s maths focus entry 28 min; reading (media) sessions correctly ignored; js/core/routines.js:628-645 (e.date !== day; no complete check), 676-678 (day = routineDay(now))
fix: Decide and document: count only sessions with metrics.complete (or full 10-minute blocks, matching the pay rule), and measure by the routine day (filter on routineDay(e.ts) rather than e.date).
rootCause: The habit reads the Goals engine's calendar-day convention inside the routine-day model.

title: Calendar: a repeating event can only be edited or deleted as a whole series; no 'this showing only', and an event cannot run past midnight
detail: The event modal edits the one record; Delete on a weekly lesson says 'This removes every showing of it' and there is no 'Skip this one' or 'Only this event' (the model already has a per-date skip list, ext.g.skip, used only for Google). Moving one week's lesson means deleting the series. validate() also refuses an end time at or before the start time, so 22:00–01:00 cannot be entered except as two events.
evidence: js/modules/calendar.js:1100-1105 (confirmDelete: whole series), 409-431 (occursOn reads ext.g.skip only), 1359-1361 (end <= start refused)
fix: Add 'Skip this showing' (a local skip list on the record, read by occursOn) and 'Edit only this showing' (skip + a one-off copy); allow an end time on the next day ('ends next day' when end < start).
rootCause: Recurrence exceptions were built only for the Google two-way sync.

title: Routine player's finish screen says '炎 1 days'
detail: The finished screen prints the streak as '炎 ' + n + ' days' with no singular, so a first kept day reads '1 days'.
evidence: eval prod2/player.js: Morning Routine played to the end → finished text 'Morning Routine kept · 7 of 7 · +23 XP · 2 gold · +4 HP · 炎 1 days'; js/modules/routineplayer.js:182
fix: Use the shared plural helper ('1 day', '2 days'), or the streak chip used elsewhere on Routines.
rootCause: Hand-built string without pluralisation.

title: A routine's time window never closes it: a Morning routine played at 19:00 is kept, paid and streaked as on time
detail: tick() checks only the routine day (canTick), never the window, so a Morning Routine with a 06:30–08:00 window can be played and fully paid at 19:03 the same day; nothing marks it late. The evening routine has an explicit late rule (until noon, flagged m.late), but a routine done hours after its window is indistinguishable from one done on time in History, the streak and Reports. setRest() by contrast does refuse once the window has closed.
evidence: eval prod2/player.js at 19:03: fromTemplate('morning') (window from the template) → player → 7 of 7, award {xp:23,gold:2}, state 'done'; js/core/routines.js:357-379 (tick: no window check), 451-452 (setRest refuses after w.to)
fix: Decide the rule: either record e.late/e.outside when the day is kept after window.to (shown as 'kept late' in History, still paid), or close the day at window end + grace for streak purposes. At minimum show 'outside its window' in the player.
rootCause: The window is used for reminders and display only, not for judging the day.

title: Daily habits editor: Save and Cancel sit inside the 'How habits work' help card, which stretches to the habit list's height
detail: On #/routines/edit/habits (Mac) the right column's second card holds the explanation paragraph and then the page's Save/Cancel buttons; the card is stretched to the list's height (content ends ~520 px of a 290 px-tall card), leaving a dead lower half, and the primary action reads as part of the help text. With the list longer than the viewport, Save scrolls away with the card top.
evidence: shots/productivity/inv/habits-edit-mac.png; measure: DEADH section.k-card 'Daily habits' used 177/319 (earlier sweep), help card 970–1446 x 366–657 with Save at y≈498
fix: Put Save/Cancel in a sticky footer under the habit list (as the routine editor does) or in the page header's action slot; let the help card size to its content (align-self:start).
rootCause: Actions appended to the last side card; cards stretch in the grid row.

title: Touch sizes on Focus setup and Routines settings: selects 39 px tall, time inputs 42 px, switches 34x20
detail: On iPad and iPhone (coarse pointer) the Focus setup's selects (Nudge, Limit, Subject, Assignment) measure 320x39 / 330x39, the objective input 40 px, the penalty switch 34x20; Routines › Settings' review time inputs 100x42 (iPad) / 64x42 (iPhone) and every switch 34x20; Reminders' sort and priority pills 161x30 / 109x30 on iPad. All below the 44 px touch minimum (invariant 69). The previously reported reminders circles (32x32) and Pacing ticks still hold.
evidence: prod2/s-ipad-__focus.json, s-iphone-__focus.json, s-ipad-__routines_settings.json, s-iphone-__routines_settings.json, s-ipad-__reminders.json (SMALL lines)
fix: Apply the coarse-pointer min-block-size token to .k-input/.k-select/.k-pill-select, and give .k-switch a 44 px hit area through its label (padding on the label, not the track).
rootCause: The touch minimum in components.css raises buttons but not inputs, selects or switch tracks.

title: Morning review summary prints '11 days away..' and lower-cases the exam's name
detail: The morning review's template line appends the first warning as title + ': ' + body.toLowerCase() + '.', but the Exams hub's season notice body already ends with a full stop and holds the exam's title, so the summary reads 'Exam season is on: revision block 24 is 11 days away..' — a doubled stop and the assessment's own title lower-cased (an 'AQA 7517 Paper 2' becomes 'aqa 7517 paper 2').
evidence: eval: KOS.reviewSheet.open('morning') → '…Exam season is on: revision block 24 is 11 days away.. A good first task: …'; shots/productivity/inv/dr-morning-ipad.png; js/core/dayreview.js:540, js/core/exams.js:1077-1078 (body ends with '.')
fix: Strip a trailing full stop before appending and do not lower-case the body (lower-case only its first letter when it is not part of a title, or reword the line).
rootCause: String concatenation that assumes the notice body has no punctuation and no proper nouns.

title: Calendar event modal: Cancel floats in the middle of the footer on a new event
detail: The footer is [Delete?] [Cancel .k-spacer] [Add event]. On a new event there is no Delete, so Cancel is the first child and gets both the dialog-foot rule (first child: margin-inline-end:auto) and .k-spacer (margin-inline-start:auto): it sits at x 643–717 in a 275–1195 dialog, neither beside the primary button nor at the start.
evidence: shots/productivity/inv/cal-modal-mac.png; js/modules/calendar.js:1442-1447; css/components.css:382 (.k-dialog-foot > :first-child:not(:only-child) { margin-inline-end: auto }), css/layout.css:363 (.k-spacer { margin-inline-start: auto })
fix: Drop k-spacer from Cancel and let the danger button carry margin-inline-end:auto (productivity.css:601 already does); or render an empty start slot.
rootCause: Two auto-margin rules apply to the same element when Delete is absent.

title: Routines Today: 'Today's three' rows clip their titles mid-letter with no ellipsis, and the ○ mark shrinks so rows misalign
detail: Each mini row is [mark 22px][title .k-rt-grow.k-ellipsis][muted]. .k-rt-grow is display:flex (column), so the title text becomes an anonymous flex item and text-overflow:ellipsis on the flex container does nothing: long titles are cut mid-glyph ('…interviews, s', 'certificate repla'). The mark has no flex-shrink:0, so long titles squeeze it from 22 to 12 px and their text starts 10 px left of a short row's ('Reminder 2' at 292 px vs 282 px).
evidence: shots/productivity/inv/rt-three-crop.png (2x), shots/productivity/inv/dawn-routines-mac.png; eval: rows → mark W12/W12/W22, title L282/L282/L292, title computed display:flex overflow:hidden text-overflow:ellipsis scrollWidth 685 > 310; js/modules/routines.js:566; css/views/routines.css:15 (.k-rt-grow display:flex), 41 (.k-rt-mark no flex-shrink)
fix: Use a plain block for single-line text (drop k-rt-grow or add .k-rt-grow.k-ellipsis{display:block}) and give .k-rt-mark flex:none. The same 'k-rt-grow k-ellipsis' pairing appears in other routine/review rows; fix it once in the CSS.
rootCause: An ellipsis utility applied to an element another class turns into a flex container.

title: Reminder alert notifications read 'Reminder · due 10 minutes to go' / 'due 1 day to go'
detail: notice() builds the body as 'Reminder · due ' + the alert label with ' before' replaced by ' to go', so every advance alert is ungrammatical: 'due 10 minutes to go', 'due 1 hour to go', 'due 1 day to go', 'due 1 week to go'. The same text is the toast, the bell item and the closed-app push (the outlook reuses notice()). An all-day reminder's 'At the time' alert fires at 09:00 as 'due now'.
evidence: eval: KOS.reminders.forecast() for a reminder due tomorrow 09:00 with alerts [10] → body 'Reminder · due 10 minutes to go'; all-day due in 2 days → 'Reminder · due now' at 09:00; js/core/reminders.js:460-464
fix: Word it as 'Due in 10 minutes · 09:00' / 'Due tomorrow' / 'Due today' from the actual offset and time.
rootCause: String substitution on the option labels.

title: Pacing 'Edit week' accepts any date as the week beginning: a mid-week date overlaps the previous week and takes over 'this week'
detail: updateWeek() only checks the date's shape and that no other week has the SAME wb. Moving w/c 9 Nov's 'Week beginning' to Wednesday 4 Nov is accepted: the week now overlaps w/c 2 Nov (2–8 Nov), keeps its label 'w/c 9 Nov', moves its 16 rows, and on Friday 6 Nov currentWeek()/weekFor() return the moved week instead of w/c 2 Nov, so the hero, carry-over, Home's plan card and lesson dating all read the wrong week. The date input in the dialog offers every day.
evidence: eval: P.updateWeek('2026-11-09',{wb:'2026-11-04'}) → returned the week {wb:'2026-11-04', label:'w/c 9 Nov'}; currentWeek() → '2026-11-04 w/c 9 Nov'; weekFor('2026-11-05') → '2026-11-04'; 16 rows moved (restored afterwards); js/core/pacing.js:445-461; dialog shots/productivity/inv/e-pacing-mac.png
fix: Snap the week beginning to its Monday (or refuse a non-Monday with a message), refuse a date inside another week's 7 days, and re-derive the default label ('w/c …') when it still matches the old default.
rootCause: The week gate validates format and uniqueness, not the week grid.

title: Pacing 'Edit week' dialog on Mac: 'My week' sits alone on its own row under 'Week beginning' while 'School week' is in the row above
detail: The fields are laid out Week beginning · Label · School week on one row and My week alone on the next, leaving two empty columns; the two week numbers that belong together are split, and the Note then spans the full width.
evidence: shots/productivity/inv/e-pacing-mac.png (dialog 375–1095 px; My week 403–616 px, nothing to its right)
fix: Two rows: Week beginning · Label, then School week · My week (or put the hint under Week beginning in a full-width row).
rootCause: Grid auto-placement with a hint paragraph that pushes the fourth field to a new row.

title: Achievement progress pings sit exactly over the section strip (Productivity/Study pills) and blend with it while fading
detail: The ping stack is fixed at topbar + 12 px, rail + 16 px — the position of the section subnav. While a ping fades in or out its text mixes with the pills underneath ('CS In the zMaths IT 1 / Study spaces' on Pacing), and while shown it hides the first pills. Seen on Pacing after Focus sessions were logged (cross-area: the achievements layer, but it covers this area's navigation).
evidence: shots/productivity/inv/pace-classdays-mac.png (top-left, 220–560 x 72–135); css/views/achievements.css:270 (.k-ach-pings position), js/modules/achievements.js:693-712
fix: Anchor pings to the bottom-left (above the HUD) or the top-right under the header chip, away from in-page navigation.
rootCause: The ping position was chosen without the section strip that occupies it on every section page.
